verdicts.why: Causing someone to have pain, elegance or an assurance is stated flatly; the verb takes no side on the giver or the thing given.
Plain transfer of possession, the neutral centre against which hand over, bestow and dole out are the loaded neighbours.
Being the source of an effect is a causal statement with no attitude toward cause or effect.
Movement toward the speaker's vantage point, the plain verb of motion with nothing said about how or why.
Arriving is reported as an event; the express, the carriage and the gentlemen simply reach the door.
An event coming to pass in due course is plain narration with no judgement of the event.
A grammatical marker of equal degree; it carries whatever the compared adjective carries and adds nothing of its own.
Emphatic negation is strength of meaning, not an attitude toward the thing negated; the speaker's feeling comes from the clause, not the adverb.
Nearness in future time is a plain temporal measure with no view of what is coming.
Doing something in a good manner is evaluative by definition, as good is; the approval is the meaning itself, not an attitude riding on top of it.
To think well of someone means to approve, and that approval is the whole meaning rather than a colour the word adds beyond it.
Knowing something pretty well is a measure of thoroughness with no stance toward what is known.
A demonstrative intensifier that borrows its force from the noun it precedes; such a story or such circumstances are coloured by story and circumstances, not by such.
Pure contrast with what was already mentioned; no attitude toward either party.
The other day is a plain marker of recent time with nothing said about the day.
Other times as the distant past is a temporal pointer; any nostalgia belongs to the sentence, not the adjective.
The continuum of experience is as neutral a noun as the language has.
A single occasion, as in the first time, is counted rather than judged.
Time as a resource one has or lacks is described plainly; having no time for speech states a shortage without blame.
The present moment, stated as a point on the clock.
The narrative now that moves a past-tense story forward is a device of sequence, not of attitude.
In these times contrasts eras without preferring one; the critic's even now judges Lady Catherine's type, not the word.

The belittling in only a clergyman comes from the meaning and nothing more measured against an expected scale, which is the gloss itself; merely is the neighbour that adds a sneer, only is the plain one.
Exclusive restriction, as in only genius knows, marks who is included and no one's worth.
The only to fail construction reports an unexpected outcome; the disappointment is in the outcome, not in the connective.
